FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (Second Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized 
by the Tobacco and Tobacco Products Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture 
Divisional Council. 


Different brands of nasal snuff are manufactured in this country varying in cost depending upon the leaf tobacco 
used, the processing employed and the admixture of various other ingredients. The range of different brands of 
nasal snuff produced in the country is very wide and it was felt necessary to lay down certain minimum standard 
specifications. The broad objective of this standard is not only to enable the Indian consumers to get the nasal 
snuff of an assured quality, but also to help in promoting export of this product. 


This standard was first published in 1962 and subsequently revised in 1973 to delete requirements of lead and 
arsenic as these increase the cost of quality control without any proportionate utility; to include requirements for 
chloride; and to bring down the maximum limit for nicotine.This revision has been undertaken in order to update 
the standard in the light of current industrial and trade practices and also to comply with the rules framed under the 
Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products Act, 2003 (COTPA). In this revision, title has been modified to clearly 
indicate that the standard deals with the specification of nasal snuff since snuff is available in many forms like dry 
and wet. Requirements of calcium and crude fibre have been deleted. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 : 1960 ‘Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)’. The number of significant places retained in the 
rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 2111 : 2018 


Indian Standard 
NASAL SNUFF — SPECIFICATION 


( Second Revision ) 


1 SCOPE 


This standard prescribes the requirements for quality, 
packing, and the methods of test for nasal snuff. This 
standard does not cover the requirements for flavour 
and aroma of snuff. 


2 REFERENCES

indicated were valid. All standards are subject to

standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility 
of applying the most recent editions of these standards.

3 TERMINOLOGY 


For the purpose of this standard, the following 
definition shall apply. 


16132 : 2014/ 
ISO 2881 : 1992 


16236 : 2014/ 
ISO 2817: 1999 


3.1 Snuff — Snuff is a generic term for fine-ground 
smokeless tobacco products available in both dry and 
moist forms. 


3.2 Nasal Snuff — The dry snuff is available in many 
forms for different ways of consumption, the one 
consumed by inhalation through nose is called nasal 
snuff. It is known by different local names in different 
parts of India, for example nasvar in North India and 
nasayam in Andhra Pradesh (see IS 10335). 


4 REQUIREMENTS 


4.1 Description 


The nasal snuff shall be prepared from tobacco leaf, 


which is processed to a very fine powder and then 
sieved through a 250 mesh sieve. It shall be free from 
irritants like pepper and ammonium salts. The nasal 
snuff is available in many varieties like plain, toasted, 
flavoured and scented. 


4.2 Freedom from Weevil Attack 


The nasal snuff shall be free from any weevil attack 
when examined by the method prescribed in 7 of IS 5643. 


4.3 Harmful Substances 


The snuff shall not contain any substances injurious 
to health as covered by the Dangerous Drugs Act, 1930. 


4.4 The material shall comply with the requirements 
given in Table 1. 


5 PACKING 


The nasal snuff shall be packed in waxed paper, glassine 
paper or any other suitable and permitted paper 
packaging. It may also be packed in other permitted 
packaging material or multilaminated pouches, glass 
or tinplate containers. The quantity packed in each 
retail package will be as agreed to between the vendor 
and the buyer. 


6 MARKING 


6.1 The following particulars shall be legibly and 
indelibly marked on each retail container in addition 
to any other prevailing statutory Rules and 
Regulations: 

a) Description of contents; 

b) Brand name, or brand code; 

c) Name and address of the manufacturer; 

d) Date of manufacture or date code; 

e) Net quantity; 

f) Any other marking required under the Legal 


Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules, 
2011; and 

g) Statutory health warnings in the manner and 
in accordance with the provisions of the Rules 


framed under the Cigarettes and Other 
Tobacco Products Act, 2003 (COTPA). 


6.2 BIS Certification Marking 


The product may also be marked with the Standard 
Mark. 


IS 2111 : 2018 


6.2.1 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the 
provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 
and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The 
details of conditions under which a license for the use 
of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers 
or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian 
Standards. 


7 SAMPLING FOR TEST PURPOSES 


Representative samples of the material shall be drawn 
as prescribed in Annex B or as agreed to between the 
vendor and the buyer. 


8 TESTS 


8.1 Tests shall be carried out as prescribed in 4.2 and 
col 4 of Table 1. 


8.2 Quality of Reagents 


Unless specified otherwise, pure chemicals shall be 
employed in tests and distilled water (see IS 1070) shall 
be used where the use of water as reagent is intended. 


NOTE — ‘Pure chemicals’ shall mean chemicals that do 
not contain impurities which affect the test results.

ANNEXA 
[Table 1, SI No. (i)] 
TEST FOR SIEVING REQUIREMENT 


A-1 APPARATUS 


A-1.1 Test Sieve—250 micron IS sieve prepared for test 
by removing any film, grease or other water repellent 
material and then drying. 


A-1.2 Analytical Balance, accurate to 0.01g. 


A-2 PROCEDURE 


A-2.1 Weigh accurately 20.0 g of the material (see B-3.2) 
dried at 100°C for 2 h and transfer it to the test sieve. 
Cover the sieve and screen the material in a Ro-Tap or 


a similar machine for 20 min. Two small rubber corks of 
size 6 are introduced alongwith the material on the sieve 
to facilitate the breaking up of any soft lumps of the 
caked material. After 20 minutes, stop the machine and 
brush the residue on the sieve, if any, into a tared 
weighing dish. Weigh the dish and determine the mass 
of the residue held on the sieve. 


A-3 CALCULATION 


Material passing through 250 micron 
IS sieve, percent by mass 


-100(1-) 
M 


where 
m = massing ofthe material retained on the test 
sieve; and 
M = mass in g of the material taken for the test.

IS 2111 : 2018 


a) Full identity of the sample; 
b) Method of sampling; and 


c) Material passing through 250 micron sieve, 
percent. 


ANNEX B 
(Clause 7) 
SAMPLING OF SNUFF 


B-1 GENERAL REQUIREMENTS FOR SAMPLING 


B-1.0 In drawing, preparing, storing and handling 
samples the following precautions shall be observed. 


B-1.1 Precautions shall be taken to draw the samples so 
as to protect the samples, the material being sampled 
and the receptacles for samples from loss or gain of 
moisture and from adventitious contamination. 


B-1.2 The samples shall be placed in clean and dry 
receptacles. The sample receptacles shall be sealed air- 
tight after filling and marked with the full details of 
sampling, date of manufacture, name of the 
manufacturer and other important particulars of the 
consignment. 


B-1.3 Samples shall be stored in such a manner that the 
conditions of storage do not unduly affect the quality 
of the material. 


B-1.4 Sampling shall be done by a person agreed to 
between the purchaser and the vendor and in the 
presence of the purchaser (or his representative) and 
the vendor (or his representative). 


B-2 SCALE OF SAMPLING 


B-2.1 All the bulk containers in a single consignment 
of the material pertaining to the same brand shall 
constitute a lot. If the consignment is declared to consist 
of different brands, the bulk containers belonging to 
the same brand shall be grouped together to constitute 
separate lots. 


B-2.1.1 Samples shall be tested for each lot for 
ascertaining the conformity of the material to the 
requirements of this standard. 


B-2.2 The number of bulk containers to be selected 
from a lot shall depend on the size of the lot and shall 
be in accordance with Table 2. 


B-2.3 These bulk containers shall be chosen at random 
and for this purpose some random number table as 
agreed to between the purchaser and the vendor shall 
be used. In case such a table is not available the 
following procedure shall be adopted. 


B-2.3.1 Arrange all the bulk containers in the lot in one 
order and count them as 1, 2,.... up to r and so on. Every 
rh bulk container so counted shall be withdrawn to 
give a sample for test where: 


r=— 
n 


N being the number of bulk containers in the lot and n 
being the number of bulk containers to be chosen. If r 
comes out to be a fractional number, its value shall be 
taken as equal to the integral part of it. 


Table 2 Number of Bulk Containers to be Selected 
for Sampling 
(Clause B-2.2) 


Lot Size No. of Bulk Containers to be Selected 
N n 
(UI (2) 
Below 5 2 
6 to 10 3 
Over 10 4 


B-3 PREPARATION OF SAMPLES 


B-3.1 Individual Samples 


The number of containers to be taken at random from 


IS 2111 : 2018 


each selected bulk container shall be sufficient so as to 
give about 180 g of the material. The material so taken 
out shall be mixed together; 90 g of the same shall be 
taken and then divided into three equal parts of 30 g 
each. Each part shall constitute an individual sample 
representing the bulk container and shall be transferred 
immediately to thoroughly clean and dry receptacles 
and sealed air-tight. The receptacles shall be labelled 
with the particulars given under B-1.2. 


B-3.1.1 The individual samples so obtained from the 
lot shall be divided into three sets in such a way that 
every set has an individual sample representing each 
selected bulk container. One of these sets shall be 
marked for the purchaser, another for the vendor and 
the third for the referee and all the three sets shall bear 
the seals of the purchaser and the vendor. 


B-3.2 Composite Sample 


From the portion of the material left over after preparing 
the individual samples (see B-3.1) equal quantities of 
the material shall be taken for each selected bulk 
container and well mixed together to form a composite 
sample of about 150 g for the lot. 


B-3.2.1 The composite sample shall be divided into three 
equal parts, one for the purchaser, another for the vendor 
and the third for the referee and all the three samples 
shall bear the seals of the purchaser and the vendor. 


B-3.3 Referee Samples 


Referee samples shall consist of a set of individual 
samples (see B-3.1) and a composite sample (see B-3.2) 
marked for this purpose and shall bear the seals of the 
purchaser and the vendor. These shall be kept at a 
place agreed to between the two. 


B-4 NUMBER OF TESTS 


B-4.1 Tests for the determination of oven moisture and 


total alkaloids asnicotine shall be conducted on each 
of the individual samples in a set (see B-3.1). 


B-4.2 Tests for the determination of the remaining 
characteristics shall be conducted on the composite 
sample (see B-3.2). 


B-5 CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY 


B-5.1 A lot shall be declared as conforming to the 
specification, when: 


a) each of the test results for moisture content, 
and total alkaloids as nicotine satisfies the 
corresponding requirements specified in 
Table 1. If, however, one or more test results 
do not satisfy the respective requirement, the 
conformity of the lot shall be ascertained in 
accordance with B-5.1.1; and 

b) the test results on the composite sample for 
the remaining characteristics satisfy the 
corresponding requirement given under 
Table 3. 

B-5.1.1 In case one or more of the test results do not 
satisfy the requirements for moisture content, and total 
alkaloids as nicotine, the following procedure shall be 
adopted for determining conformity of the material in 
respect of these characteristics. The mean and the range 
of the corresponding test results shall be calculated as: 


_ Sum of the test results 
Mean) Number of the test results 


Range (R) = Difference between the maximum and 
minimum of the test results. 


B-5.1.2 The appropriate expressions as shown in col 6 
of Table 3 shall be calculated. If the values of these 
expressions satisfy the relevant conditions as given in 
col 6 of Table 3, the lot shall be deemed to have satisfied 
the requirements for moisture content, and total 
alkaloids as nicotine.

Review of Indian Standards 

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 


‘BIS Catalogue’ and ‘Standards : Monthly Additions’.
